comments.content: 1. **[Critical] integration-tests/extensions-install.test.ts:28** — The test unconditionally uninstalls a globally installed extension named `test-extension`. If a developer already has a real extension with that name, running the integration test deletes it and never restores it. Extensions are installed in the user-level extension directory, not the rig workspace. [Extension documentation](https://google-gemini.github.io/gemini-cli/docs/extensions/)

2. **[High] integration-tests/extensions-install.test.ts:14** — The fixed, generic name shares a global namespace across test workers. If two invocations using `test-extension` run concurrently, one invocation’s initial or final uninstall can remove the other invocation’s extension between its install, list, and update commands, producing nondeterministic failures or updates against the wrong source.

3. **[High] integration-tests/test-helper.ts:323** — `stdin` is ended only when a truthy string is supplied. The update call at `extensions-install.test.ts:42` supplies no input, so when update requests confirmation it waits forever on an open pipe and the test hangs until the runner times out. Passing `stdin: ''` has the same defect. The later upstream test supplies confirmation input to update. [Upstream test](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/integration-tests/extensions-install.test.ts)

4. **[High] integration-tests/extensions-install.test.ts:50** — Uninstall and rig cleanup are not in guaranteed teardown. If installation succeeds but the list assertion, update command, or update assertion fails, execution never reaches lines 50–53; the globally installed extension and test directory remain and contaminate subsequent tests.

5. **[High] integration-tests/test-helper.ts:315** — The spawned process has no `error` listener. If `node` cannot be resolved from `PATH`, or the working directory disappears before spawning, the child emits an unhandled `error`, crashing the Vitest worker instead of rejecting the returned promise.

6. **[High] integration-tests/test-helper.ts:324** — The writable stdin stream also has no error handler. If the child exits immediately while supplied input is being written—for example, startup fails before reading the install confirmation—the pipe can emit `EPIPE` as an unhandled error and terminate the test worker.

7. **[Medium] integration-tests/extensions-install.test.ts:48** — The update is verified only by searching command output for the target version. If update prints “available version 0.0.2” in a prompt or status message but cancels or otherwise leaves the installed manifest at `0.0.1` while exiting successfully, the test passes without an update occurring.

8. **[Medium] integration-tests/test-helper.ts:329** — Appending each `Buffer` directly to a string decodes chunks independently. If a multi-byte UTF-8 character is divided between stdout chunks, it becomes replacement characters in the returned result, so assertions against Unicode CLI output fail even though the child emitted valid UTF-8.

9. **[Medium] integration-tests/test-helper.ts:336** — The same chunk-wise decoding corruption affects stderr. A multi-byte character split across stderr chunks produces a mangled success result or rejection message.

10. **[Low] integration-tests/extensions-install.test.ts:40** — `toContain('test-extension')` does not establish that the exact extension was listed. If the target is absent due to a listing regression but another installed extension is named `test-extension-helper`, the assertion passes.

11. **[Low] integration-tests/test-helper.ts:352** — On nonzero exit, stdout is discarded even though many CLI paths render their error text there. If a command prints `Extension test-extension was not found` to stdout and exits 1 with empty stderr, callers receive only `Process exited with code 1:` and lose the actual failure reason.

12. **[Low] integration-tests/test-helper.ts:343** — Signal termination is misreported because the close listener ignores its signal argument. If the child is killed by `SIGKILL` or `SIGTERM`, the rejection says it exited with code `null`, concealing the real cause.

13. **[Low] integration-tests/extensions-install.test.ts:53** — The test directory is deleted unconditionally after cleanup. With `KEEP_OUTPUT=true`, a successful run still removes this test’s artifacts, defeating the integration harness’s retained-output mode and leaving no files for post-run diagnosis.
